page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.114-456 is an x86_64 virtual machine configuration powered by AMD EPYC 7J13 processors clocked at 2.55 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 114 dedicated physical CPU cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, providing a total of 228 vCPUs. It includes 456.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a strict 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage devices, and it comes provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

By maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration across 228 vCPUs, this instance maximizes multi-threaded processing density over raw memory allocation per thread. Architectural constraints dictate that all block and file persistent storage must be attached remotely over network fabrics, requiring network-based I/O planning. This configuration is tailored for large-scale parallel processing tasks, high-concurrency microservices, massive CI/CD compilation workloads, and compute-bound simulations that demand high CPU core counts without massive per-thread memory overhead.

Operating at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core, this configuration emphasizes high compute density over per-thread memory footprint. The instance lacks local storage drives and hardware GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent data workloads. It includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With extensive parallel CPU capacity, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.114-456 is suited for distributed computing, intensive continuous integration pipelines, batch processing engines, and large-scale compute-bound services.
